question: In September 2023, Wallonia granted a building permit for a project at Belgium’s École provinciale d’agronomie et des sciences de Ciney (Ciney Provincial College for Agricultural Studies and Sciences) involving plans to tear down, rather than renovate, the establishment’s oldest structure – a period farmhouse with aesthetic and historic features – and replace it with a new concrete building.

The project received an EU grant under the European recovery plan. The press reported that the demolition was necessary in order to meet energy renovation standards and therefore qualify for EU support. The energy efficiency of a building is crucial. 1.

Do renovation projects, particularly those aimed at improving a building’s energy performance, qualify for support under the European recovery plan, or is it necessary to build a new building to benefit? Does the Commission believe the heritage of the property should be taken into consideration?
Did the Commission’s services have to give an opinion on this file before the demolition and reconstruction decisions were taken?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.1.2025) Renovations to improve a building’s energy performance qualify for support under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The total estimated expenditure in energy efficiency in buildings under the RRF is EUR 81.1 billion in the EU, of which EUR 67.5 billion for renovation and EUR 13.5 billion for new construction1.
Belgium’s Recovery and Resilience plan (BE RRP) includes investments of over EUR 1 billion in the renovation of buildings2. The Commission recognises the importance of preserving cultural heritage.

According to the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive3 and the Energy Efficiency Directive4, Member States may exempt buildings officially protected as part of a designated environment or because of their special architectural or historical merit from renovation requirements. A measure in the BE RRP is I-1.

09 ‘Renovation of public buildings – schools’ covers light, medium and deep renovations, as well as demolitions and reconstructions. It is mentioned that demolition/reconstruction would apply to buildings that are in most cases prefabricated and where renovation is not possible due to their dilapidation5.
The BE RRP did not provide any indication regarding protected buildings as part of a designated environment or because of their special architectural or historic merit. The RRF is performance-based.

After receiving a payment request, the Commission assesses whether the actions completed comply with the requirements of the Council Implementing Decision6 before paying out the respective amount to the requesting Member State. The Commission does not give an opinion on individual projects before they start. Investment I1.09 will be assessed under the fifth and sixth payment request by Belgium, expected in 2026.
